canal_p24_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_001.text: The fifty-sixth morning arrived without bells beyond the ordinary round. Yue woke before Luo and listened to a cart taking the sound longer route behind the sheds. The old sale notice still hung by the landing, its edge curled from eight weeks of weather. She washed, ate from her own provisions, and put on the mended coat. Today was closure, not departure. Her booked road began tomorrow, leaving this day for the last accepted work and an evening in which she could say goodbye without running for a boat.

canal_p24_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_002.text: A pale mark on the keeper's wall showed how high a damp coat had once hung after the storm. Nobody had scrubbed it away successfully. Luo noticed Yue looking at it and said she had considered covering it with the winter rota. "Then whenever I lose the rota, I would find the storm again." The keeper left the stain uncovered. Its presence proved less than an official water gauge and more than a room could pretend never happened. Yue accepted a cup of tea and waited while Luo packed the actual morning-round bag.

canal_p24_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_003.text: Yue's stage-four practice remained steady and limited. She had made no new cultivation pair during the canal term and would carry no commission fuel into the road. Rest had restored ordinary concentration after work; it had not turned external apparatus charge into a stronger body. She stretched her shoulders without sending a command anywhere. Bao's wrist had taught the town enough about patience for one season. Outside, the young keeper called that the lower mark was clear. Luo answered with the ordinary agreed words instead of checking whether Yue was listening.

canal_p24_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_004.text: The final receiving interval began at the practical route board. Yue compared the current named receivers with their actual replies and the safe approaches with the accepted notices. The damaged old step and outer return remained closed, the longer winter alternative usable under its recorded condition. Its separate repair estimate had an acknowledged route-office reference, no promised date. The officer received the current copies on his standing round. Yue signed for the comparison she actually completed. The work did not require her to repair a second whole bank before the commission could end.

canal_p24_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_005.text: At the dry shed Luo and the young keeper inspected the case seals, disconnected fittings, and separate stone box. Their receiving record preserved the exact selected balances, with two hundred forty-four units the conservative floor across earlier choices. No new draw had occurred since the accepted last small test. Eight stones remained commission property. Jiang's appointments had ended; future powered work required a funded qualified operator and measured rated conditions. Yue handed over no secret key. The keeper's named custody and alternate were already recorded, and the young woman's supervised access matched her actual appointment.

canal_p24_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_006.text: The wage clerk opened Yue's ordinary account before the last report check. Ten equivalents and twenty cumulative copper had already been accepted and paid, including earlier portions used for food. Two remaining equivalents were now represented by actual completed closing intervals, subject to the final receiving signature. Four copper would settle the ordinary total at twenty-four after that signature. Her separately completed emergency appointment had earned six under its own funded labor line. The clerk did not add another twenty-four to the prior twenty because closure looked more celebratory with a large pile.

canal_p24_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_007.text: The ordinary worker account totaled twenty-eight scheduled equivalents at two copper each, fifty-six in all. Yue's twelve, Bao's four and a quarter, the mason's one and three quarters, Jiang's three, An Ru's two, the tow crew's three, Tian's one, and the short observer, garden, and reed tasks completed the allocation. Those last shares were one half, one quarter, and one quarter. Completed work and approved transfers supported each line; Yue's final receiving signature was still due. The carpenter's injury had changed who finished a task, not created another invisible worker.

canal_p24_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_008.text: The twenty-eight material copper and twelve for six charged stones matched actual purchases and received stock. With fifty-six ordinary labor copper, including the last four prepared for settlement, they reconciled the ninety-six repair allocation. Reused path pavers were recorded inventory, not a second cash purchase. Remaining sound materials stayed in commission custody. The initial one hundred twenty served its actual division: twenty-four to the valid loan and ninety-six to work. Pei prepared the earmarked cash closing entry, to be completed after Yue's final wage payment rather than prematurely erasing the four still in its envelope.

canal_p24_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_009.text: The separate thirty-six emergency copper had paid twenty-four labor, eight materials, and four for two new charged stones. Its eight equivalents at three each were Yue two, Jiang two, Bao one and a quarter, and the trained road workers two and three quarters after the injury transfer. Their real readiness, travel, and work intervals matched the accepted appointments. The unused dangerous tasks had not become unpaid orders to households. The emergency account stayed separate from ordinary repairs. Pei checked the totals and asked the clerk to stop calling every closed account a victory.

canal_p24_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_010.text: The ordinary two-month operating book closed at thirty-five actual receipts and thirty-four actual costs. Twenty-eight had covered accepted current standing and temporary service, six the official messages and archive passages. Its thirty-six budget had been a cap; two unused authorized copper did not exist as extra cash. The real one-copper balance remained after the last service payment. Yue compared the final boat entries with their receipts, keeping prior prepaid uses separate. The last current service worker signed the one-copper payment that had still been due yesterday. This account could now leave the forecast behind.

canal_p24_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_011.text: The one actual operating copper was transferred by the trustees' current authority to maintenance. Beside it already stood the one-copper wrong-cart material reimbursement, bringing the present maintenance cash to two. The emergency's original eight-copper material cost remained visible; reimbursement had not undone that expenditure or created two refunds. Future six-copper monthly reserve shares depended on actual toll collections. Two current copper could not repair every closed edge or fund a larger emergency. Luo counted them and said she preferred a small true purse to a splendid one whose contents lived only in the clerk's adjectives.

canal_p24_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_012.text: The separate four-copper merchant grant remained held for the accepted limited winter record post. Two merchants had actually contributed two each. The assistant's short intervals would earn two per month for two months after closure, with a stated end date and no unpaid automatic continuation. Current closing-week work belonged to its own administrative allowance. Pei received the winter grant count with the assistant present. Neither put it into the projected eighteen monthly toll copper or spent it again as gate reserve. The broad shelf labels had already made the office less dependent on Pei's eyes.

canal_p24_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_013.text: The quarry outcome retained its own receiving records: nine private copper delivered four-three-two to the households and two separately paid to the regular permit authority. Its proved narrowing, accepted correction, bounded high-water inference, and future enforcement contact stayed together. The earlier ten-copper hardship gift and twelve food sacks were separate support, with no hidden waiver. The garden, reed, and stall households approved their chosen public descriptions. Yue checked the actual recipients before tying the copy. A closure report could say what was paid and still admit what the season had taken beyond that payment.

canal_p24_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_014.text: Han's private deposit account was already complete. Thirty-two reserved copper, including the actual twenty-four public debt payment and eight private customer receipts, plus sixteen from the private hoist and plank sale had repaid the conditional forty-eight. Its authorized receiver had released the listed private security. The spare property sale had not transferred workers' tools or the common bed. Today's final file preserved that completion rather than reopening the refund because Han disliked leaving. He signed receipt of his copy and kept it in the private chest whose return had begun a smaller future.

canal_p24_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_015.text: The valid public loan stood at fifty-six: two hundred forty advanced, one hundred twenty-eight repaid in old cash, thirty-two in returned unused timber credit, and the current twenty-four paid. Its eligible actual-receipts term would allow four per payable month after costs and reserve needs, requiring fourteen payable installments. The private gear lease and keeper fee each proposed four monthly under their accepted defined service conditions. Future gross eighteen remained a forecast, not cash received today. New watches, repairs, or operators needed actual appointments and funds; a winter closure would require lawful review rather than free labor.

canal_p24_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_016.text: The final household count was twenty-four approvals and four retained objections among the twenty-eight current responses. The actual written replies and accepted proxies stayed with the count. Some disliked the tariff; others feared voluntary work would leave future maintenance short or wanted debt service delayed further. Their objections remained readable. Ordinary lawful water access would continue under the same posted rules, not be withdrawn as punishment for dissent. The chair asked the clerk to read the amended text before signature. Yue watched Tian's mother lean forward to hear the work clause clearly.

canal_p24_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_017.text: The charter recognized the completed four annual maintenance seasons, sixty accepted worker-days each, two hundred forty in total. Current work would be offered and accepted on stated terms. No birth, marriage, absence, or old cash balance revived the finished pledge. The common bed, marked routes, and diversion use remained outside private loading title; lawful private goods remained their owners' property. Named receivers, current boundary notices, actual accounts, and review routes replaced convenient assumptions. The chair signed the approved text under the actual household responses. The four dissenting comments were fastened beside it, where no celebratory copy could omit them.

canal_p24_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_018.text: The public comparison went beneath the landing eave in broad lettering. Old pledge complete; current jobs finite; valid debt bounded; private gear distinct from common routes. The ordinary tariffs remained posted on their own board. A pilot asked whether the new charter lowered his fee. Luo said no and pointed to the tariff. The pilot looked disappointed, then asked when tomorrow's first passage would run. The keeper answered from the schedule. Yue liked the transition. A useful charter could leave a person still wanting a cheaper boat and able to book the actual one.

canal_p24_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_019.text: The winter task board showed real contacts, accepted jobs, and unanswered invitations as different things. The former check worker's short upstream rope inspection had been completed and paid by its own employer at the posted price. It was not a public winter salary. The laundry contact remained available for priced work, and the assistant's funded post had a finite term. Pei left no "willing hands" notice without hours or rate. The check worker read the board before going home and asked to keep his contact current. The clerk accepted that actual request without promising the season.

canal_p24_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_020.text: The common practical boundary copy was delivered to the private wharf and cabinet shed. Han's crane kept its reduced accepted sweep clear of the public wall. Temporary storage beside the return needed a current permission and visible end date. The cabinet maker's shed threshold remained private despite the invited inspection through it. His next-month rent amendment stayed with the actual parties. The public title question did not seize their goods or solve their entire account. Yue handed over the last current route copy and let the tenant return to his finished table.

canal_p24_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_021.text: Luo received the next-month service plan with the young keeper present. Their short defined rounds and actual alternates remained, while night emergencies or loaded repairs required fresh priced authority. The future eighteen-copper gross estimate would be checked against real traffic and costs before new commitments. If conditions exceeded routine service, they would close the affected use or obtain another funded appointment. The current plan did not make nearby households permanent spare workers. The girl asked who would tell an impatient pilot this. Luo said she would, and the girl could point to the board if the pilot failed to listen.

canal_p24_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_022.text: The dry apparatus handover included its actual rated upper-pocket condition and accepted movement. It had never been a machine for taking the whole force of the flood into Yue's arms. The exact charge sheets stayed with the eight stones, the fitting notes with the disconnected frame, and the receiving keys with their named custodians. Its current two hundred forty-four conservative floor was a comparison across earlier routes, not a replacement for selected readings. Bao's observer note and the mason's actual adjustment remained separate. The keeper received useful work, not the promise that Yue would return whenever it felt frightening.

canal_p24_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_023.text: The lower ground withdrawal remained the first available response when the position or water left accepted limits. Full spoken instructions and actual receivers mattered more than anybody's cleverness with a bell. The safe house route allowed the grandmother's real walking pace; the reed shelter contact followed its seasonal household. The new low barrier marked the damaged return for children as well as readers. Yue walked the sound approach with the officer one final time. He would hold the separate repair estimate. She would not carry a closed edge in her pack as a reason to abandon every later road.

canal_p24_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_024.text: The standing officer received the quarry enforcement contact and the closed-return notices within his actual role. Private correction and public follow-up had their own dates. Future reports could reach a named person who knew which upstream outlet and which lower reach were meant. The current garden losses did not authorize unlimited digging on every private bank. The storm findings were bounded, and that boundary kept the next request from becoming an accusation nobody could test. Luo read the receiver number aloud and copied it onto the ordinary gate sheet where she would actually use it.

canal_p24_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_025.text: Bao attended the short seated closing interval his wrist still allowed. He watched the unloaded receiving check and signed only his actual observation. Loaded carpentry remained barred despite improved motion. His priced private drawing review for next week stayed a limited sitting appointment; his sister would help him follow the clinician's current limit without turning every argument into treatment. The qualified mason had completed the physical public adjustment under the approved quarter-day transfer. Bao congratulated him directly. The words sounded uncomfortable and therefore entirely real. Yue offered him tea without making the cup into a test of recovery.

canal_p24_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_026.text: Tian brought the confirmed loft terms and told Luo the actual trial would begin on the seventieth day, six paid weeks with named lodging and ordinary return travel. The plant would stay in the keeper's window under their small accepted arrangement. Her mother would be the alternate if it needed another place. Tian had passed the real fitting after stopping and correcting the fold, and chosen the trial herself. She would not follow Yue to the forest. The seamstress put her hand against the pot and said goodbye to the gate leaf as if it might sensibly answer.

canal_p24_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_027.text: After final approval Han took the old sale notice down himself. He did not tear it into heroic scraps. Pei retained the needed source copy; he kept his own under the completed private account. The empty patch on the landing board looked smaller than Yue expected. Han rubbed the place where the nail had been and said the timber beneath it would need ordinary patching. Luo told him not to submit the whole board as a private loss. He laughed, then looked toward the canal's common bed without trying to calculate what a buyer might pay for it.

canal_p24_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_028.text: Han's wife came to collect his public receiving copy and carry home the lunch he had forgotten. The private letters remained with their family, damaged gaps visible. Their smaller store and loading work would depend on actual winter business and the accepted gear service. Nobody promised prosperity as a reward for correcting the notice. Yue thanked both spouses for keeping the public and private accounts clear. Han said either kindness was useful, and his wife told him to eat before evaluating it further.

canal_p24_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_029.text: Luo handed the young keeper the ordinary round bag without checking each object again. The girl knew its current contents, key access, and limits. When she left, the principal keeper stood very still. Yue asked whether she felt replaced. "For twenty minutes," Luo said. "Then she will bring the kettle back wrong and I will have a purpose." The joke covered a quieter feeling. Yue stayed beside her without promising another visit to fill it. The gate had work after the apprentice departed, and Luo had begun letting somebody else truly do part of it.

canal_p24_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_030.text: Pei showed Yue the broad final folder labels. The assistant could find the charter, debt account, permit outcome, and route closures during her funded intervals. After two months, continuation would require actual support and acceptance. The older clerk had agreed to stop before tired eyes made copying dangerous. Yue asked whether she wanted a last report read aloud. Pei said she wanted the lamp moved and the young woman fed. The instruction was specific enough to follow. Yue moved the lamp, then closed the folder instead of reopening it to prove she could still help.

canal_p24_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_031.text: Qiao Lan's personal correction remained beside the collective completed pledge, with the aunt's chosen reply acknowledging its receipt. Missing song lines had not been filled with invented certainty. The niece collected the approved public copy during her ordinary errand and hummed the surviving part under her breath. Tian recognized a fragment and joined for three notes before losing the tune. Nobody asked the children of old workers to sing as proof they owed another season. Yue listened from the office door, letting the imperfect little sound carry a name whose place had finally stopped depending on her memory.

canal_p24_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_032.text: The gardener left closure early to tend the seed he had actually bought. The reed household went back to its repaired roof and diminished stock. The stall owner opened the smaller batch she had priced. Their food grain, hardship gifts, and bounded quarry contributions remained theirs under the received terms. Their losses were not declared nonexistent. Yue watched the separate departures and understood why no single final speech could fit them. The charter had changed what could be demanded. These people would decide what to attempt with the next season that still belonged to their work.

canal_p24_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_033.text: In the apprentice room Yue returned the borrowed bowl to its shelf and checked her personal pack. Survey pegs, reference rules, public source copies, keys, frame, and charged stones had gone to their actual holders. Her clothes, tablet, ordinary food, mended coat, and retained personal arrangement could travel. The roll Tian had sold her held her own small things. She took no optional commission object that the next place would need to understand. Luo inspected the room doorway and asked whether she had found the missing spoon. Yue pointed to the kettle, where the keeper had left it.

canal_p24_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_034.text: Ren's actual accepted appointment was the fifty-ninth morning, the third after today's closure. The full review interval had patients and staff confirmed. Yue's requested return had finally become a real place in their calendars. It had not yet become a physical visit. The actual retained earlier arrangement would govern what she owed and what questions remained; no exclusive promise was attached to every possible past. Yue placed the acceptance where she could reach it at the orchard pavilion. She would have to hear answers from living people, rather than treating the letter's tidy date as the repair itself.

canal_p24_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_035.text: The three-copper ordinary fare for tomorrow and the following day was already paid from her cumulative earned ordinary wages. Two personal copper for beds and two for food stayed reserved. The optional west-kiln connection would use one additional personal copper if she chose that route, fitting the same two travel days. The ordinary passage agent had confirmed the actual stages and current contingency contact. Yue checked the receipt, then put the road purse away. The public repair allocation did not owe the fare. Her future accepted appointment had a journey she could actually afford.

canal_p24_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_036.text: Any overdue personal orchard return under her retained arrangement remained unfinished until she arrived and performed the review with Ren. Other arrangements retained their different duties and papers with Ren. Yue knew correspondence had corrected scheduling, not outcomes. The admission no longer felt like a clever boundary she could hide behind. It was the reason to go. She would leave after completing the canal term and arrive rested enough for the accepted interval. The forest commission beyond the orchard was a separate future beginning, with no canal realm award or borrowed apparatus waiting in her pack.

canal_p24_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_037.text: The personal itinerary allowed ordinary days fifty-seven and fifty-eight on the road, and actual orchard arrival on fifty-nine. A serious interruption would need a real message and changed arrangement, not a desperate unpriced sprint. Today no interruption had been reported. The passage receiver held the booked place. Yue told Luo where a genuine message could reach her while traveling, then pointed out the ordinary canal contacts that should answer canal questions first. The keeper accepted the distinction. She did not turn the travel address into another emergency appointment purchased by affection.

canal_p24_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_038.text: There remained three ways to finish the consequences of Yue's stay. She could spend the evening preparing the public comparison's traveling receiving copies for their actual offices. She could complete the dry workshop handover as a last practical service, leaving every commissioned object in place. Or she could take the priced west-kiln connection during the same two-day journey, seeing home briefly before Ren's appointment. The work choices would finish tonight inside closure; the home choice used tomorrow's road. Each would leave something different done and something different left to the named people already here.

canal_p24_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_039.text: The final report receiving signature was given after the actual checks, source transfers, and closure reading. Yue's twelve ordinary equivalents were now wholly accepted, including the two closing equivalents she had completed in their named intervals. The ordinary labor allocation remained fifty-six and twenty-eight equivalents in total. The clerk marked no social visit as another workday. Bao's recovery and Tian's fitting stayed in their real private arrangements. Yue put down the pen and felt the day's work end in her hands. She could choose an evening or a road without pretending either was still owed to the public wage book.

canal_p24_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_040.text: The clerk paid the remaining four ordinary copper. With the cumulative twenty previously received, Yue's ordinary wage total was twenty-four. The six emergency copper had been settled separately under the completed two-equivalent appointment. She checked the receiving line before putting her own coins away. The personal fare and four road-provision copper were already handled from her earned ordinary funds; she did not pay the fare a second time to celebrate leaving. Luo watched her close the purse and said the town had finally managed to purchase precisely as much apprentice as it had hired.

canal_p24_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_041.text: The current maintenance cash was two, the winter record grant four held for its stated future work, and the commissioned charge in its selected readings. The original repair and emergency accounts were closed at their actual expenditures. The public loan remained fifty-six, with future payment tied to eligible actual receipts. These facts would belong to the next month's people, not become optional prizes for Yue's final choice. Pei put the receiving copies on their proper shelves. Yue resisted checking the knots again. The assistant could open them. That was part of what they had worked to make possible.

canal_p24_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_042.text: The fifty-sixth evening came cold and clear. At the lock, Luo's plant-care cup stood beside the ordinary kettle; at Tian's room, the real sail was gone with its customer; at Bao's house, the drawing board waited under a supported hand. Han's empty notice space would acquire current cargo information tomorrow. Yue looked at each place without demanding one last meeting from its occupant. Her road remained booked for the next morning. The charter was approved, the wage earned, and the next review accepted. She could now choose what mattered most to finish personally.

canal_p24_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_043.text: Yue still entered and left Qi Gathering stage four. The canal had sharpened her judgment and tired her shoulders, but no external stone had awarded her a realm. Her actual commands had been bounded parts of rated apparatus work; ordinary people and ground routes had carried the rescue's larger burden. She had been wrong, corrected, useful, frightened, and sometimes funny without meaning to be. The recollection made her smile. At the orchard she would be an apprentice with retained duties again, not the owner of a story entitled to decide how everyone else remembered it.

canal_p24_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_044.text: Luo brought Yue a small supper bought from her own household stock and asked which final path she had chosen. She was prepared to witness the public or workshop receiving, and prepared to say goodbye if Yue wanted home. Tian had left a note wishing her a safe ordinary road. Bao's note said to sit when tired. Han's contained the current office contact rather than another request. Yue folded the notes into the personal part of her pack. She owed no answer grand enough to repay eight weeks of company. She could make one real choice.

canal_p24_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_045.text: With the charter approved and all accepted work paid, Yue chose her final consequence: public receiving copies, a completed dry repair handover, or the priced brief home stop. The first two would finish before the same booked departure. The third would use the extra personal copper within the two confirmed travel days. Every route would reach Ren's actual fifty-ninth morning with her habitual pack and stage-four cultivation. The people at the canal would keep their current objects, duties, and different futures. Yue put her hand on the chosen invitation and stood.

choices.text: Finish the public comparison copies and their receiving.
Leave a clear dry fault index with the actual workshop keepers.
Take the priced brief west-kiln home stop on the booked road.

canal_p24_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_046.text: Yue chose the public copies and sat beneath the landing eave with Pei's assistant. The approved comparison, actual charter count, and current boundary notices lay on clean boards. Private loss details and family pages stayed in their proper files. The final official dispatch had already been booked and paid within the operating message account; no new fare appeared after closure. Yue checked each packet's actual destination while the assistant wrote broad receiving labels. Luo brought the lamp. She complained that the moths would take this as another appointment and immediately attracted three.

canal_p24_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_047.text: The first local receiving copy went to the winter task board, where the former check worker read the finite-job clause and left his current contact. The laundry woman checked the notice position beneath the eave. Nobody received a winter salary merely by approving the paper. Yue stood beside the board while two pilots argued over the unchanged tariff. She answered one actual question about the completed pledge and let Luo answer the operating schedule. The record had begun to travel through different mouths. It no longer needed every explanation to sound like its apprentice author.

canal_p24_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_048.text: At the private wharf Han read the current property comparison under his own lamp. The crane's reduced movement, actual lease condition, and valid fifty-six debt were as clear as the common bed's limit. He signed receiving without adding a demand for praise. His wife attached the copy where the foreman would find it before loading. Yue saw that practical placement and thanked her. Han asked whether the county office would read it kindly. Yue said the signed source and scope could help it read accurately. He accepted the smaller word.

canal_p24_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_049.text: The cabinet maker received the route notice from the sound public approach. His apprentice had finished the private rack, and the common strip remained clear. The damaged edge and old step stayed visibly closed, with the ordinary authority's estimate acknowledgment on the public copy. Yue did not walk the hollow ground merely to prove she was leaving it responsibly. The tenant put the notice by the door where future workers would enter. He offered her a small wooden stool as a gift. She thanked him and declined the bulky object. Its usefulness could stay with someone who sat here.

canal_p24_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_050.text: The official dispatch receiver took the traveling comparison packets in their paid ordinary carriage. Yue witnessed the local acceptance, not an invented arrival at the county registry that night. The assistant would track the actual later receipt through its office contact. Original source books stayed with their holders. This choice left a public record moving beyond the town while leaving the truth of its delivery open to confirmation. Yue put her pen away. She did not carry the packets onto her own road or make the orchard wait for an office she had not been hired to visit.

canal_p24_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_051.text: A gardener stopped at the public board after supper and read the enforcement contact aloud. He asked if he might copy it onto his seed wrapper. Yue gave him a clean scrap instead. He laughed at the small extravagance and wrote the number himself. His current losses were still real, his nine-copper fund share had been four, and his next season remained his attempt. The document did not demand gratitude to keep its protection. He nodded once at the removed sale notice's empty place. The nod seemed less like forgiveness than a person discovering room to think about something else.

canal_p24_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_052.text: Yue returned to Pei with the actual local receiving signatures and dispatch acceptance. County receipt remained pending. The assistant knew its next follow-up and the limited paid intervals in which to perform it. Pei found the broad label without asking Yue where she had hidden the paper. "You may now leave," the clerk said. Yue laughed, then felt tears threaten unexpectedly. Pei pushed the lamp away from her face and told her to drink water. The practical kindness let both women avoid a speech neither wanted to hear herself make.

canal_p24_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_053.text: On the fifty-seventh morning Yue boarded the paid ordinary passage with her habitual pack. Luo came to the sound landing to see her off after arranging her current round with the named alternate. Tian had local work and sent a brief note. Bao's sister waved from the path; he was resting. Han stayed at his private store. The boat pushed away without a final assembly. Yue watched the broad comparison board become a pale rectangle beneath its eave. Her public choice had left something people could read while she was elsewhere, which was precisely its point.

canal_p24_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_054.text: The fifty-eighth day brought the confirmed hill walk and second paid night. Yue used the food and bed copper she had reserved, without pretending the road provided free meals because she had helped a town. The route's ordinary covered rest place proved useful when a short shower passed. She had no packet needing another detour and no borrowed device demanding return. At the night's stop she reread Ren's accepted interval and the actual retained duties. The county copy's later receipt belonged to its named clerk. Tomorrow Yue would answer a different table in person.

canal_p24_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_055.text: By the last night before the orchard, the public outcome had its real limits: local copies received, traveling packets accepted by the paid carrier, later county receipt still tracked by the canal office. No private claim detail or family letter had traveled in Yue's pack. The canal's approved record could stand without her retelling it at every inn. She set her personal road purse beside the bed and checked the morning walk to Ren's pavilion. The fifty-ninth appointment was near enough to be a place rather than an intention. She slept before composing another explanation.

canal_p24_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_056.text: Yue chose the dry repair handover and brought the accepted fault notes to the shed. Luo and the young keeper agreed to a brief ordinary evening review, not a new powered appointment. The disconnected frame stayed covered beside the sealed charged store. Yue wanted the first failed trial's wet wick and misread reference to remain easy to find among later successful notes. She had no right to remove her early error simply because the charter had ended well. The keeper lit a lamp, and the young woman spread the actual copies on the dry bench.

canal_p24_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_057.text: They made a short fault index from existing accepted notes: changed cloth condition, reference position, guard stop, measured head, and receiver withdrawal. It described where to look in the source sheets rather than promising a machine that diagnosed itself. The young keeper asked why Yue's first mistaken assumption deserved its own line. Yue told her how quickly an earlier good result could make a person impatient with new evidence. Luo said the apprentice ought to write that in larger letters. Yue did, then let the younger woman choose the plain wording she would actually remember.

canal_p24_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_058.text: The dry case's cover tie was sound, its fittings unloaded, its stops already accepted in the closing check. They made no new pulse and altered no rated part. The young keeper compared the sketch with the actual disconnected selector from the safe ordinary inspection position. Her limited access did not make her a qualified powered operator. Future use still required a funded appointment and the measured condition. Yue watched her find the correct source line without help. The useful consequence was a clearer path from a doubt to a stopping decision, not another supply consumed to make an evening impressive.

canal_p24_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_059.text: Bao's approved observer note remained with the actual mason's adjustment record. His light description had helped identify the bracket question; the other worker had performed the physical change. Their names did not merge into a single workshop legend. Luo read the injury restriction and said she would not ask Bao to demonstrate a loaded turn at his next visit. Yue copied that practical reminder beside the drawing. The young keeper pointed out that Bao would probably offer to prove himself without being asked. The reminder therefore needed to be readable by whoever heard the offer.

canal_p24_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_060.text: The fuel calculation remained exactly as selected by earlier work. Two hundred forty-four was the conservative floor across routes, with actual meter readings controlling custody and future use. Eight stones stayed in the commission's marked box. The fault index did not add a new draw, divide their charge arbitrarily, or claim a storm had replenished them. Yue wrote the final no-draw receiving date and checked it against today's closing record. Luo signed the new index's receipt. Its usefulness would be tested by a future question, not by an unappointed trial made now to justify writing it.

canal_p24_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_061.text: The young keeper put the index on the shelf beside the case, then asked Yue to pretend she had forgotten which stop mattered. Yue played an impatient customer requesting a larger pulse. The girl found the rated-condition sheet and refused the request. Luo applauded with exaggerated delight until the girl pointed to the line saying a principal keeper was bound by the same condition. Yue laughed. The exercise ended dry, ordinary, and brief. It had given the custodian a sentence she could use against familiarity as well as strangers, leaving the commissioned objects untouched.

canal_p24_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_062.text: When they closed the shed, Luo retained the named key and the young keeper knew her supervised access. The new fault index stayed with their receiving copy. Yue carried none of it onto the road. This choice had left a clearer workshop record and a custodian who had practiced finding a stop condition, while the wider public dispatch remained in its ordinary office process. There was no promise that Yue would return as winter's unpaid operator. Luo thanked her, then asked her to take the empty tea cup back to the stove room. The ending required ordinary carrying after all.

canal_p24_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_063.text: The fifty-seventh morning began at the same booked passage. Yue left the key, source sheets, frame, and stone box with the canal, boarding only with her personal things. Bao sent word approving the fault index's preservation of the failed trial, which mattered more to her than praise for the successful one. Tian waved from her workroom window. Luo returned to the gate after the actual farewell. The boat's ordinary motion carried Yue away without a new command. She watched the receiving shed roof disappear behind the grain house and let its next question belong to its named people.

canal_p24_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_064.text: During the fifty-eighth day's hill walk Yue met a traveler whose cart wheel had loosened. His own hired driver inspected it from sound level ground. Yue offered no unrelated qi repair and kept to her booked route once they had the ordinary help available. At the second paid night's stop she unfolded Ren's acceptance. The full interval and actual patients awaited her on the fifty-ninth morning. She had left a bounded workshop record at the canal and brought no powered proof of usefulness. At the orchard she would need to listen before deciding whether any familiar technique answered the problem.

canal_p24_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_065.text: The last night before the orchard was quiet enough for Yue to hear another traveler's kettle boil. Her repair outcome had left the dry index received, the selected charge intact, and custody with the people actually appointed. The damaged common edge still had its separate ordinary estimate; its closed condition had not been erased by a satisfying workshop evening. Yue checked her habitual pack and the morning approach to Ren's pavilion. The accepted physical review was close. She put the papers away and slept, prepared to arrive with the limited trained body and unfinished obligations she truly possessed.

canal_p24_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_066.text: Yue chose the brief home stop and told Luo before the last supper cooled. The west-kiln connection cost one extra personal copper and fitted the confirmed fifty-seventh and fifty-eighth travel days. Ren's fifty-ninth morning remained accepted. The public records and dry apparatus were already received by their named holders; her choice did not leave them secretly waiting for a final command. Luo said the old kiln people might feed her better than the keeper had. Yue disagreed, then admitted she had no current evidence. The keeper accepted the honest correction and cut her another slice of turnip.

canal_p24_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_067.text: On the fifty-seventh morning Yue paid the additional copper to the confirmed connecting-cart receiver and boarded the ordinary booked boat stage. Her three-copper main fare had already been paid, with food and beds provisioned separately. The detour would end at the named return connection before the night's stop; it was not a promise to improvise a road later. Yue checked the actual departure time once and let the receiver keep the working copy. She took her habitual pack. Nothing commissioned from the canal traveled home disguised as a gift proving how far she had risen.

canal_p24_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_068.text: The west kiln stood under a dull haze that smelled of hot clay before Yue saw its chimney. She had spent seven years trying to cultivate after ordinary shifts here. The yard seemed smaller without becoming kinder: stacked tiles, ash by the firing shed, the old wheelbarrow with a replacement handle. A woman who had shared those shifts looked up from sorting and stared. "You learned to come back," she said. Yue laughed, surprised by how sharply the simple sentence found her. She had arranged this stop for herself, not because another household had submitted a claim.

canal_p24_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_069.text: They sat beneath the familiar shed eave while the current workers took their ordinary break. Nobody asked Yue to lift the hottest load or supply magical fire. One younger worker wanted to know whether cultivation made fatigue disappear. Yue answered from her actual stage-four body and the sore shoulders she had brought off the canal. The older woman said she had never needed a realm to know Yue carried baskets badly when distracted. Yue protested, then watched a worker use the sound handle and changed her complaint into a question about the new wheelbarrow's balance.

canal_p24_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_070.text: The old sorting table held a fresh repaired leg. Its maker was proud enough to show Yue the joint and irritated enough to correct her first description. She listened. Here she was remembered for missed shifts, earnest diagrams, and ash caught in her hair, not only a successful public hearing. She spoke about the canal when asked, keeping the borrowed fuel, ordinary rescue, and private household stories within their actual limits. She did not perform a command to make the account more impressive. The worker said a safely finished path sounded useful. Yue was glad that was enough.

canal_p24_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_071.text: The woman who had shared her shifts asked whether the orchard people Yue had just mentioned expected her soon. Yue said the fifty-ninth morning was now actually arranged, with the full review interval and ordinary journey paid. Any physical visit still owed remained ahead. The woman nodded without congratulating her for writing letters. "Then go when you said." They ate a simple paid meal from the kiln cook's current batch, using Yue's own road food provision. Its burnt edge tasted familiar. Yue finished it, laughing when someone offered a dog the less edible crust.

canal_p24_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_072.text: For a short personal interval Yue helped sort a light row of cooled ordinary tiles at the invitation of the worker already handling them. It was a voluntary familiar gesture, not a new kiln shift or paid task she had failed to price. When the heavier stack arrived, she stepped aside and let the current appointed crew use its proper handling arrangement. The older woman teased her about becoming sensible. Yue said she preferred the word "occasionally." The little stop let her remember work that had begun before anyone called her an apprentice worth listening to.

canal_p24_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_073.text: She left before the confirmed connecting cart departed. There was no new promise to stay through winter or return on an unexamined date. She asked where a later personal letter would reach the old coworker and offered her own actual future contact when known. They embraced with clay dust between their coats. At the cart Yue paid no second detour fare; the extra copper already covered the accepted connection. She looked back once at the chimney. Home had given her a conversation and a meal, not another object or obligation that the orchard would have to understand.

canal_p24_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_074.text: The cart rejoined the route in time for the first reserved night. On the fifty-eighth day Yue took the confirmed hill walk and used the second bed and remaining food provision as planned. She did not squeeze the visit longer by skipping rest or imagining qi would mend a late arrival. Her personal money had covered the extra kiln connection; no public allocation paid it. At the night's stop she reread Ren's full interval. The short return to familiar work had made the next physical return feel more possible, which was useful without claiming that either had already been completed.

canal_p24_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p24_075.text: By the last night before the orchard, the home outcome had its real result: a priced brief kiln visit inside the two confirmed travel days, an ordinary shared meal, and departure without another vague promise. The canal's public copies and apparatus remained with their appointed people. Yue had her habitual pack and stage-four cultivation, with no borrowed charge or new companion. Ren's actual fifty-ninth morning lay at the end of the next short approach. She rested her hands on the folded acceptance, then put it away. Tomorrow she would finally cross the pavilion threshold in person.

canal_end_public.speaker: narrator
canal_end_public.text: On the fifty-ninth morning Yue reached the orchard pavilion's approach with her habitual pack and Qi Gathering stage four. The canal's local comparisons had been received; its traveling copy belonged to the paid carrier and the clerk tracking actual delivery. Ren's accepted full review waited inside the orchard, with the real retained arrangement and any physical return still to be completed. Yue looked at the familiar roof through autumn mist. She had left a public record behind. Now she would enter a conversation that required her own presence.

canal_end_repair.speaker: narrator
canal_end_repair.text: On the fifty-ninth morning Yue reached the orchard pavilion's approach with her habitual pack and Qi Gathering stage four. The canal frame remained disconnected with its selected charge intact, fault index received, and custody held by the named keepers. Ren's accepted full review waited inside the orchard under the real retained arrangement; any owed physical return still required today's work in person. Yue heard someone moving a stool beneath the pavilion roof. She had left useful stopping words behind. Here she would begin by listening before proposing another repair.

canal_end_home.speaker: narrator
canal_end_home.text: On the fifty-ninth morning Yue reached the orchard pavilion's approach with her habitual pack and Qi Gathering stage four. The paid brief kiln stop had fitted the two confirmed travel days, leaving no new borrowed object or vague promise on the road. Ren's accepted full review waited inside under the real retained arrangement, with any owed physical return still to be completed by arrival and work. Yue brushed a last trace of clay dust from her sleeve. Home had let her return once. The pavilion doorway asked her to do it again.
